sections.h2: Where is the Marathon County Register of Deeds and how do I reach it?
sections.html:
The Marathon County Register of Deeds is in the Marathon County Courthouse at 500 Forest Street, Wausau, WI 54403. Call 715-261-1470 or fax 715-261-1488. The office records real estate documents such as deeds, land contracts, mortgages, satisfactions and assignments.

Hours change around holidays and closures, so confirm them by phone before you drive in with an original deed. The county page for the week of November 2, 2026 showed shortened days and a Friday closure, with normal hours resuming Monday, November 9.

The county also accepts documents by mail, which suits a seller who lives out of town and cannot visit the courthouse.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Marathon County itself?
sections.html:
Marathon County is the largest county in Wisconsin by land area, at about 1,545 square miles, and the fourth largest by total area. It was founded in 1850 from part of Portage County, and Wausau is the county seat. The Wausau metropolitan area is made up of the county, and a county park marker shows the spot at 45 degrees north and 90 degrees west, the center of the northern half of the Western Hemisphere.

The Census Bureau counted 138,013 residents in 2020 and estimated 139,432 in July 2025, a gain of 1.0 percent. Health care and social assistance receipts reached about $2.09 billion in 2022, and retail sales were about $3.65 billion.

  • Housing units: 62,059 (July 2025 estimate).
  • Owner-occupied rate: 73.3 percent (2020 to 2024).
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $219,600.
  • Median gross rent: $999 a month.
  • Median household income: $77,884.
  • Mean commute: 19.1 minutes.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 348.

Several smaller communities sit outside Wausau, among them Athens, Edgar, Marathon City, Mosinee, Rothschild, Spencer and Stratford, all of which have a Marathon County Public Library branch. A house in any of them is recorded at the same office on Forest Street.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Marathon County?
sections.html:
Recording a real estate document costs $30. The county adds a $1.00 certification charge per filed document, and copies of recorded documents run $2 for the first page and $1 for every page after that. Emailing recorded documents carries the same per-page charge as copies. The state transfer fee is separate and is paid at the time you submit the deed.

Make the $30 check payable to Register of Deeds. If there is a transfer fee, submit it at the same time.

sections.h2: How do I record a deed by mail in Marathon County?
sections.html:
The county lays out a short sequence for a property transfer. It does not offer legal advice, so questions about the deed language go to an attorney or an abstract company.

  • Prepare the deed, notarized or authenticated, with a full legal description when it names specific parcels of land.
  • File the Wisconsin electronic transfer return with the state and print the receipt, which appears on the second screen after you submit.
  • Include the $30 recording fee payable to Register of Deeds, plus any transfer fee.
  • Mail everything to Register of Deeds, 500 Forest Street, Wausau, WI 54403.
  • List your email address. Since January 1, 2026, documents come back electronically unless you enclose a self-addressed, stamped envelope.

The deed also needs the name of the drafter and the name and mailing address of the person it should be returned to. If an out-of-state form is the only one you have, the county says you may attach a cover sheet that supplies the title, return address and parcel number in the proper places.

sections.h2: What formatting rules apply to Marathon County deeds?
sections.html:
Wisconsin Statute 59.43(2m) sets a standard document format, and the Marathon County office applies it. A document that misses the standard can be refused. The county lists these points:

  • Leave the upper right corner blank, at least 3 inches by 3 inches, for the recording stamp.
  • Put the name and return address directly under that area, or on the left within the top 3 inches.
  • Place the parcel identifier number directly under the return address.
  • Keep the title inside the top 3 inches, outside the blank corner.
  • Use white, standard weight, letter or legal size paper with black ink so the page scans.
  • Keep a top margin of at least half an inch on every page and other margins of at least a quarter inch.
  • Do not hinge the pages.

State law also bars the office from recording a document that contains an individual's Social Security number, so remove it before you send the deed.

sections.h2: How do I search Marathon County land records online?
sections.html:
Since September 3, 2019, Marathon County has used the Ascent Land Records Suite from Transcendent Technologies, and land and tax information is posted at ascent.co.marathon.wi.us/ascentlandrecords. The real estate index can also be searched free in LandShark. Viewing or printing a recorded document there costs a fee.

Surveys are held by the county surveyor, whose number is 715-261-6000. The surveyor's online folders cover benchmarks, section summaries, plats of survey and tie sheets, sorted by town and range. A pre-sale check of the recorded chain of title and any survey is worth doing before you sign a contract.

Records requests follow the same rule as other Wisconsin government records. The county page says the presumption is that a record is open for public inspection, and a denial must come with specific reasons. A person who is denied can start a court action to compel disclosure.

sections.h2: Which Marathon County forms help with inherited property?
sections.html:
The Marathon County recording page lists several forms that come up when an owner has died: a Personal Representative Deed, a Designation of TOD Beneficiary, a Termination of Decedent's Interest form with instructions, a Quit Claim Deed form and a Warrant Deed. Transfers by will, descent or survivorship are exempt from the state transfer fee under Wis. Stat. 77.25(11), and the exemption reason must be written on the deed.

A sale by the heirs to a buyer afterward is a new conveyance. The fee under Wis. Stat. 77.22 applies to it at 30 cents per $100 of value, with the seller owing it.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Marathon County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The phone number is 715-261-1470, and the fax is 715-261-1488. The office is at 500 Forest Street, Wausau, WI 54403. Call ahead for current hours, because the county posts temporary schedule changes.

faqs.q: How much is the recording fee in Marathon County?
faqs.a: It is $30 per document for real estate records. Certification adds $1.00 per filed document, and copies cost $2 for the first page and $1 for each added page. Any state transfer fee is paid in addition.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed to the Marathon County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the deed, the printed transfer return receipt and a $30 check payable to Register of Deeds to 500 Forest Street, Wausau, WI 54403. Add any transfer fee and an email address. Documents are returned electronically unless you enclose a self-addressed, stamped envelope.

faqs.q: Is there a Wisconsin transfer fee when I sell a Marathon County house?
faqs.a: Yes, unless an exemption applies. The seller owes 30 cents for each $100 of value under Wis. Stat. 77.22. For a $219,600 sale, near the county median home value, the fee is about $659. Exempt transfers include those by will, descent or survivorship.

faqs.q: Where can I look up Marathon County recorded documents online?
faqs.a: Use LandShark for the real estate index, which is free to search, and the Ascent land records site at ascent.co.marathon.wi.us/ascentlandrecords for land and tax information. Viewing or printing a recorded document through LandShark costs a fee.
